plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any bid below your value risks losing the auction to a slightly higher bid, even if it's below your value, resulting in zero profit. Bidding above your value risks winning but paying more than the item is worth to you. Since this is round 1 and there is no history, I will bid my true value.

Since all bidders are rational, and values are between $0 and $20, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. In a symmetric equilibrium, each player bids (2/3)*value. However, my value is $24, which is outside the possible range. I should bid my true value, as any lower bid risks losing the auction to someone with a lower value, and any higher bid risks overpaying.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges on bidding slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $20, the expected value is $10. To win reliably against rational opponents, I should bid slightly above $10, but considering my value is $18, I can bid higher. I will bid $17.5 to maximize my chances of winning while minimizing overpayment.
